chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, the Exalted, has assigned seventy thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). They are disheveled and covered with dust, sending blessings upon him every day from the day he was killed until what Allah wills, meaning the rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him). They pray for those who visit him, saying: 'O Lord, these are the visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do this for them and do that for them.'

key_terms.زُوَّارُ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): The visitors of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)
key_terms.قِيَامَ الْقَائِمِ (ع): The rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the role of the angels at the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) regarding those who visit him?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the cosmic significance of Karbala by noting that seventy thousand angels, described as 'shu'than ghubran' (disheveled and dust-covered) to signify their humble devotion, continuously intercede for visitors from the day of martyrdom until the rise of the Qa'im. This tradition underscores the enduring spiritual connectivity between the living and the Ahl al-Bayt, framing ziyarah not merely as a physical act but as a participation in the celestial worship of the Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn Walīd narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from ‘Ali ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Basīr, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Allāh, the Exalted, has dedicated seventy thousand angels to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) who are disheveled and covered with dust who send blessings on him every day since the day he was killed (and will continue to do so) until a time that Allāh wills – referring to the rising of the Qā`im (Twelfth Imam (a.s.)). They pray for those who come to his Ziyārah by saying, “O Lord! These are the visitors of Ḥusain (a.s.)! Do this for them and do that for them.”
